title: Phone Number Parser
story: Your contact import tool reads phone numbers from a CSV, but the data is messy — some entries are '555-1234' (missing area code), some are 'abc-def-ghij', and some are completely blank. You need a parser that enforces the 'XXX-XXX-XXXX' format and rejects anything else.
why: Format validation with substring extraction and digit checking is the universal pattern for parsing structured text like phone numbers, ZIP codes, and serial numbers.
analogy: A phone number parser is like a ticket inspector on a train. The ticket must be exactly the right size (12 characters), have perforations in the right places (dashes at 3 and 7), and every section must contain only numbers — if any section has letters, it's a fake ticket.
try_it: Test valid: '555-123-4567', '800-000-0000'. Test invalid: '5551234567' (no dashes), '555-ABC-4567' (letters), '55-123-45678' (wrong lengths), '555--12-4567' (double dash). Add support for the '(XXX) XXX-XXXX' format with parentheses. Parse and return the area code separately.
tips: Use `string.str_slice(s, start, end)` where `start` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive — slice(0, 3) gives indices 0, 1, 2
The `is` keyword checks a Result's variant without extracting the value — `area_num is Err` is cleaner than a full match
Check length BEFORE slicing — if the string is too short, `str_slice` would fail with out-of-bounds errors
common_mistakes: Confusing index positions — dashes are at 0-based positions 3 and 7, which are the 4th and 8th characters (1-based)
Using `==` to compare Result to Err — use `is` instead: `area_num is Err` not `area_num == Err`
